chunks: Desirable battery characteristics. The question: What are some desirable characteristics in a battery?
A good battery stores a lot of energy for its size and weight, can deliver high current without its voltage collapsing, and lasts many cycles.
It should also lose little charge when idle, work in hot and cold, be safe, charge quickly, and cost little.
You cannot have everything, so what counts as best depends on the product.
You want a big jug (energy), a wide spout so water pours fast (power), a tight lid so it does not leak when stored (low self-discharge), and a body that survives years of use (cycle life).
A wider spout usually means thicker walls and less space inside. So raising power tends to lower the energy. Every real battery trades one for another.
At 5C (10 amps), a 30 milliohms cell keeps about 92% of its voltage, the 50 milliohms cell about 86%, and the 150 milliohms cell only 59%, and burns 15 watts as heat ((10 amps)² times 0.
15 ohms). At 1C the spread is only a few percent (98% vs 92%), which is why a capacity quoted at a low rate hides the difference.
Energy density: energy stored per kilogram (Wh/kg) or per liter (Wh/L). Internal resistance: the cell's own resistance. Low is better for high current.
Cycle life: how many charge-discharge cycles it lasts before capacity falls to a set level. Self-discharge: the charge a battery loses while sitting unused.
Specific power: the power it can deliver per kilogram.
Take a 7. 4 watt hours cell that weighs 50 g. Its energy density is 7. 4 over 0. 05 equals 148 watt hours/kg. Now draw 2 amps through an internal resistance of 0. 1 ohms.
The voltage sags by 2 times 0. 1 equals 0. 2 volts, and the cell makes 2 squared times 0. 1 equals 0. 4 watts of heat. A lower resistance would sag less and heat less.

"Desirable: high energy density, so it's small and light for the runtime; low internal resistance, so it can deliver high current without sagging or heating; a flat, stable voltage; long cycle life and low self-discharge; wide temperature range; fast charging; safe under abuse; and low cost with the right form factor.
They trade off: more energy usually means less power, life or safety, so which ones matter depends on the product."
